How LifeUSA Uses Hubstaff Today

A management review of how LifeUSA uses Hubstaff today, including team-member activity, project reporting, current gaps, and recommended next steps.

Sep 5, 2026, 5:03 PM UTC

Report contents

  1. Executive summary
  2. Team member performance view
  3. Team member details
  4. Organization-wide usage
  5. Projects and task detail
  6. Manual time and application usage
  7. Governance and controls
  8. Recommended next steps
  9. Scope and limitations

Executive Summary

  • I reviewed Hubstaff at both the team and individual levels. The report now shows each current member's recorded hours, working days, manual time, main project, and any point that may require management follow-up.
  • LifeUSA already has a useful project-level view. The organization recorded 5,288.53Source for 5,288.53Source: Hubstaff data used for this reportTable: reports/support/hubstaff-2026-08-20/analysis.json hours from Aug 4–Sep 4Source for 4Source: Hubstaff data used for this reportTable: reports/support/hubstaff-2026-08-20/analysis.json, 2026, an increase of 3.8%Source for 3.8%Source: Hubstaff data used for this reportTable: reports/support/hubstaff-2026-08-20/analysis.json from the previous equal period.
  • 40Source for 40Source: Hubstaff data used for this reportTable: reports/support/hubstaff-2026-08-20/analysis.json current members recorded time, 1Source for 1Source: Hubstaff data used for this reportTable: reports/support/hubstaff-2026-08-20/analysis.json fewer than the previous period. 18Source for 18Source: Hubstaff data used for this reportTable: reports/support/hubstaff-2026-08-20/analysis.json established members recorded no time, so management should confirm whether they are inactive, exempt, or working outside Hubstaff.
  • The main gap is the lack of task-level detail. 0.0%Source for 0.0%Source: Hubstaff data used for this reportTable: reports/support/hubstaff-2026-08-20/analysis.json of recorded time was linked to a Hubstaff task, so management can see the project but not the specific activity, case, campaign, or deliverable.
  • I recommend starting with three practical actions. Add simple task categories to the largest projects, review significant manual-time exceptions, and agree how LifeUSA will use attendance, timesheets, application tracking, and screenshots.

How each team member recorded time during the month

Each point represents one of the 40Source for 40Source: Hubstaff data used for this reportTable: reports/support/hubstaff-2026-08-20/analysis.json current team members who recorded time. The horizontal position shows the number of working days recorded, while the vertical position shows total recorded hours. The dashed lines mark the middle of the group and make unusual patterns easier to identify.

Team members noticeably outside the main range should be reviewed with their manager. The first questions should cover schedule, leave, role, project assignment, and whether time-recording expectations were followed consistently.

How to read these figures

Team recording coverage is the percentage of established team members who recorded time during the period. Recorded hours are the hours captured in Hubstaff. They provide useful management visibility, but they should be reviewed together with completed work, results, deadlines, and quality. The main reporting period is Aug 4–Sep 4Source for 4Source: Hubstaff data used for this reportTable: reports/support/hubstaff-2026-08-20/analysis.json, 2026, compared with Jul 3–Aug 3Source for 3Source: Hubstaff data used for this reportTable: reports/support/hubstaff-2026-08-20/analysis.json, 2026 and Jun 1–Jul 2Source for 2Source: Hubstaff data used for this reportTable: reports/support/hubstaff-2026-08-20/analysis.json, 2026, two earlier periods of equal length. The reporting window includes the full day of September 4, 2026. Later approved time edits may change historical totals.

Recommended next steps

Next 30 days

  1. Confirm the status and time-recording expectations of the 18 established team members with no recorded time.
  2. Run a task-tracking trial in MEMC, Programs, Donor Services.
  3. Agree when manual time requires a manager's review.
  4. Decide whether LifeUSA will manage attendance and timesheets in Hubstaff.
  5. Approve a written policy for application tracking and screenshots.

Days 31 to 60

  1. Standardize project and task names.
  2. Link projects to the existing team or remove the unused team setup.
  3. Review the projects with no recorded time (IT) and archive any that are no longer needed.
  4. Begin issuing a short weekly management summary.

Days 61 to 90

  1. Automate approved weekly and monthly reports through Hubstaff's API or CLI, subject to plan and access.
  2. Agree suitable reporting benchmarks for each department and role.
  3. Consider Hubstaff's read-only MCP option for leadership reporting once account access is confirmed.
  4. Decide whether access to detailed audit logs would justify moving to the Enterprise plan.

Decisions management needs to make

  • Which roles are required to record time, and which are legitimately exempt?
  • Which three to seven task categories would help management understand the work completed within each project?
  • Is Hubstaff expected to support payroll, attendance, costing, project management, or only time visibility?
  • Who may review screenshots and application data, for what purpose, and for how long?
  • Which weekly decisions should the future management report support?

Scope and limitations

  • Recorded hours show time captured in Hubstaff. A complete performance review should also include responsibilities, completed work, results, deadlines, and quality.
  • The reporting window includes the full day of September 4, 2026. Later approved time edits may change historical totals.
  • Application-use totals cover Aug 20–Sep 4Source for 4Source: Hubstaff data used for this reportTable: reports/support/hubstaff-2026-08-20/analysis.json, 2026 and should not be compared directly with the 32Source for 32Source: Hubstaff data used for this reportTable: reports/support/hubstaff-2026-08-20/analysis.json-day hours total.
  • Keyboard and mouse activity percentages were not available in the data reviewed.
  • No attendance or timesheet records were available for the reviewed period. This does not rule out their use at another time.
  • Audit-log information was not available under the current access, so this report does not assess organization-wide administrative changes.
  • The figures passed 17Source for 17Source: Hubstaff data used for this reportTable: reports/support/hubstaff-2026-08-20/analysis.json checks covering calculation accuracy, completeness, consistency, and sensitivity.
